title: Briefing for 2026-09-20
intro: Good morning. Here is your briefing for 2026-09-20: US markets, global news, and the Philippines, in five minutes.
us: Consumer sentiment is in the dumps despite a solid economy. Goldman Sachs blames 'lower happiness'. Why Japan’s markets flipped the usual script after central bank rate hike. Bank of England defies Fed’s rate-hike lead, leaving rates unchanged. 'Science fiction': Transport companies — the backbone of economy — are sounding alarm on fuel prices. Consumers hit by one-two punch of oil and rates from Iran war. The estimated bill is $1,700 per household. UK inflation jumps to 3.1% as energy costs soar.
global: Converse pulls 'deeply upsetting' advert after backlash. Trump says US will form 'AI Force' and appoint an artificial intelligence tsar. Trump signs sweeping Russia sanctions bill. 'We simply don't know' - JP Morgan struggling to forecast oil prices due to Trump's war with Iran. Flight chaos caused by 'millisecond' software defect, report says. Warren Buffett steps down after six decades at Berkshire - 'Father Time always wins'.
philippines: Asian Games open in Nagoya with glitzy ceremony after troubled buildup. Greenland, Denmark say US deal will not cede sovereignty. James Reid is finally home, and he’s right where he wants to be. LIST: Community events, activities on 54th Martial Law commemoration.
outro: That's your briefing. Have a great day.
